meeting_header:
Date: 2026-11-22 | Time: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 64 minutes
Attendees: Avery Clarke (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Lopez (Redwood CSM); Dana Morales (CTO, Lumos), Ethan Park (Sr ML Eng), Priya Singh (PM), Oliver Grant (Infra)
summary: POC scoping to define success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks and timelines. Focus on integration approach: OpenAI-compatible endpoints, SDK usage, tool/function calling, structured output, and on-prem/VPC considerations. Agreed to run a benchmark pilot with sample datasets and to follow up with security docs and infra planning.
transcript:
00:00 Avery Clarke: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We've got about an hour. quick intros?
00:08 Dana Morales: Hi I'm Dana, CTO at Lumos, we run a multi-tenant observability platform for ML pipelines.
00:14 Ethan Park: Ethan here, I own the inference infra and model ops.
00:18 Priya Singh: Priya, PM for our assistant product.
00:21 Oliver Grant: Oliver, infra lead.
00:23 Avery Clarke: Great. I'm Avery from Redwood, AE, and Samir is our solutions engineer.
00:27 Samir Patel: hey all. quick agenda: success criteria, load/size, perf targets, then integration details — SDKs and OpenAI-compatible endpoints and tool calling.
00:36 Dana Morales: that's perfect. we're mainly evaluating for a 6-8 week pilot to prove latency and cost targets plus ability to run in our VPC later.
00:44 Priya Singh: and we need structured JSON outputs for our downstream parsers, so structured output support is key.
00:51 Samir Patel: noted. can you give ballpark qps and tokens per request?
00:55 Ethan Park: for our assistant we'd be around 120 qps peak during batch jobs, average 25 qps steady. tokens vary — prompts ~300 tokens, generation ~400 tokens avg. some longer analytic runs up to 2k tokens.
01:08 Samir Patel: ok good, that helps. for a POC we normally pick representative flows — short chat (300/400), medium synth (1k), long analytic (2k) — and run stress benches.
01:18 Priya Singh: success criteria: 95th pct latency under 450ms for chat, cost per 1k tokens below $0.70 (hosted eq), and output schema match rate > 98% on structured fields.
01:31 Dana Morales: and security: we need SOC2, SAML SSO, KMS for keys and audit logs retained 1 year. also data residency — EU region required for a subset of customers.
01:45 Samir Patel: on security we support SOC2, SSO via SAML/OAuth, KMS integrations (AWS KMS/HSM). For private we can run in your VPC or on-prem; audit logs and retention configurable. we'll share whitepaper.
01:58 Oliver Grant: quick Q on KMS — do you require bringing your own key (BYOK) or can we use Redwood-managed?
02:04 Maya Lopez: We support both; BYOK via customer KMS is available for private deployments. For hosted there's a managed option but we can do dedicated with BYOK.
02:14 Ethan Park: regarding deployment — we're leaning dedicated or private due to compliance; what's the lift for integrating your SDK vs OpenAI-compatible endpoint?
02:23 Samir Patel: our SDKs are idiomatic (Python/Node/Go). we also provide an OpenAI-compatible REST endpoint for easy swap — same calls as openai.ChatCompletion/create-like endpoints. Function/tool calling is supported; we have examples for structured output and schema enforcement.
02:40 Priya Singh: can you run through an example for tool/function calling? we're using a set of internal tools (search, run-query, dashboard-open).
02:47 Samir Patel: sure. we support function calling payloads like OpenAI's function_call — you declare functions in the request and model returns a structured call. sometimes the transcription shows as 'function call' or 'tool call', but essentially you get back JSON with name and args. our SDK handles invocation or returns the call so you can execute locally. there's also a "structured output" option where you pass a JSON schema and the model returns JSON matching that schema.
03:12 Ethan Park: any differences in latency or token usage when using function_call vs raw text?
03:18 Samir Patel: minimal token overhead for the metadata; latency depends more on model and sequence length. function calling helps downstream parsing so usually reduces end-to-end engineering cost.
03:27 Dana Morales: benchmarks — what will Redwood run, and what do you need from us?
03:31 Samir Patel: we'll run microbenchmarks on hosted first to get baseline, then replicate on Dedicated/Private if you want. we need sample prompts, sample dataset (anonymized), target concurrency, and expected sequence distributions. we'll run throughput (tokens/sec), p50/p95/p99 latency, error rates, and cost estimates per 1k tokens.
03:51 Priya Singh: timeline — can we do a 6-week pilot? first week setup, weeks 2-3 benching, weeks 4-5 integration and schema validation, week 6 review and decision.
03:59 Avery Clarke: that map sounds reasonable. we'll propose a concrete schedule after today's call.
04:04 Oliver Grant: network wise — for private we need a peering/VPC setup, firewall rules, and a checklist for ports. do you have a template?
04:12 Maya Lopez: yes we'll provide a VPC peering checklist and infra runbook. for on-prem there's an installer package and offline options.
04:20 Ethan Park: SDK question — we have existing code built against OpenAI SDK. how smooth is migration?
04:25 Samir Patel: since we offer OpenAI-compatible endpoints, you should be able to point your existing client with minimal changes — mostly endpoint and API key. for function calling and structured output, we have helper utilities in the SDK that mirror openai SDK patterns, plus extra helpers for batching and cache hints.
04:41 Priya Singh: caching — you mentioned KV cache earlier; is that client-side or runtime? how does prefix caching work?
04:48 Samir Patel: it's runtime — we maintain KV cache for generation to accelerate repeated prefixes. there's also response caching and client-side sticky keys for session affinity. caching is configurable per-route.
04:58 Dana Morales: ok. about model choices — we plan to use an open LLM. do you recommend quantized variants for cost savings?
05:05 Samir Patel: yes, for many production workloads quantized 4-bit models strike a good balance. Redwood Optimize can recommend profiles per workload. we'll include quantization perf comparisons in the benchmark doc.
05:18 Priya Singh: structured output enforcement — how do you evaluate schema match rate? we need >98% as mentioned.
05:24 Samir Patel: we run schema validators against outputs and track match rates. for edge cases we can use model prompting + verification step. we can also run evaluators over sample prompts and provide accuracy metrics and false positives.
05:36 Ethan Park: what's the expected infra for a private deployment handling our peak? (120 qps, mixed token lengths)
05:43 Samir Patel: rough calc — depends on model size. For a 13B quantized model, you'd likely need a small fleet of dedicated GPUs with autoscaling; we can dimension more precisely after we see token/sec from your samples. we'll provide a sizing spreadsheet.
05:56 Dana Morales: any help with benchmarks we should run on our side?
06:00 Samir Patel: yes, run representative integration tests hitting the OpenAI-compatible endpoint; capture end-to-end latency including your upstream services. Also run bulk parse tests for structured outputs and tool invocation flow to validate orchestration.
06:14 Priya Singh: about monitoring — can we get token-level billing and per-route latency breakdowns?
06:18 Maya Lopez: yes Console gives token/success/cost breakdowns per token, route, and model. we can set up dashboards and tracing hooks into your APM.
06:27 Oliver Grant: encryption at rest — support for CMEK?
06:30 Maya Lopez: yes, customer-managed encryption keys are supported for private. for hosted we have service-managed keys by default but can enable CMEK for Dedicated.
06:38 Dana Morales: fine. are there any blockers from Redwood side to start pilot?
06:40 Avery Clarke: just a handshake on scope and sample data; we'll need a short contract for pilot terms (data usage, timeboxed eval). can share a standard POI pilot agreement.
06:50 Ethan Park: what about function calling latency — any benchmark numbers?
06:53 Samir Patel: we'll include p95 numbers in the perf sheet; expect similar latencies to chat requests with slight overhead for additional tokens.
07:00 Priya Singh: if we use the SDK, will we need to change invocation for streaming responses?
07:04 Samir Patel: SDK supports streaming and chunked responses similar to OpenAI SDK. examples in repo: https://redwood.ai/docs/sdk and a github samples repo link we'll share.
07:14 Dana Morales: okay, let's talk success criteria recap — Priya's items plus security.
07:18 Priya Singh: 95th pct latency under 450ms (chat), cost per 1k tokens target, and structured output match >98%. Also SSO, KMS/BYOK, and EU residency for subset.
07:29 Avery Clarke: agreed. we'll build a benchmark plan mapping tests to those criteria and a pass/fail definition.
07:35 Samir Patel: next steps: I'll produce the benchmark config and perf spreadsheet; Avery will send pilot agreement and pricing; Maya will set up infra checklist; Ethan will share sample prompts and data.
07:49 Dana Morales: timeline sounds good — we aim to start next Monday (2026-11-29) pending paperwork.
07:55 Avery Clarke: perfect. thanks everyone. we'll follow up with links and schedule.
07:59 Priya Singh: thanks.
08:01 Meeting end.
